newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares fall as Iraq euphoria goes flat.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares fall as Iraq euphoria goes flat.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell on Sunday for the first time in a week as brokers judged a wave of optimism over renewed trade with Iraq to be premature.

They said worries that Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba might lose out to Turkish and Gulf routes in the competition to handle an expected surge in Iraqi imports were behind the market's fall on Sunday from nine-month highs.

The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.60 percent to 151.97 points, dampening recent gains which followed Iraq's announcement that it had reached agreement with the U.N. for implementation of its $2 billion oil-for-food deal.

Brokers said the market got a bout of jitters from a front page local newspaper report which reprinted comments by Iraqi traders last week that Iraq would divert its trade to suppliers in the Gulf offering "better quality and cheaper" goods.
"They got panicked," said one broker, who asked not to be named. "That's what they were responding to."

Jordan, a traditional trading partner of Iraq and a transit route for many of its imports, has suffered from the six-year U.N. sanctions on its neighbour. Jordanian industry lost a major export market and business at Aqaba plummeted.
Last week investors piled into industrial stocks in anticipation of renewed business with Iraq.
"Today may be was an over-reaction. I expect the market to pick up again by the end of the week," said financial consultant Mohammad Abdullah of Pearl Consulting.
Overall stocks in 35 companies fell on Sunday. Shares in seven companies, mainly banks, rose but were unable to stem the tide of falling industrials stocks.

Jordan Industrial Resouces, Unified Co Jordan Selpho-Chemicals, and Union Chemical and Vegetable, all of which rose strongly in recent days, were all hit by Sunday's wave of pessimism, closing down at 1.32 dinars (down 0.05 dinars), 1.77 dinars (down 0.08 dinars) and 0.98 dinars (down 0.04 dinars) respectively.
Another six firms were traded but closed unchanged.

Turnover of 1.46 million dinars ($2.06 million) maintained the market's surge in volume. Total trade in the week following Iraq's food-for-oil announcement has matched turnover for the whole of the preceding month.
The private Pearl Index of 45 best-traded shares fell 0.46 percent to 81.61, 14.56 percent down on last year.
